categories.title: Plan
categories.summary: Work out what to do before anyone builds it.

categories.title: Test
categories.summary: Plan tests, write them, and keep the suite healthy.

categories.title: Investigate
categories.summary: Find out what happened or why, read-only and cited. A fix goes to Bug.

categories.title: Analyze
categories.summary: Understand code and requirements, read-only, every claim cited.

categories.title: Judge
categories.summary: Get a verdict on a change, a risk or a choice, from a seat that did not make it.

categories.title: Create
categories.summary: Documents, pages, demos and messages, grounded in your work.

categories.title: Estimate
categories.summary: Estimate effort and price, and model what runs will cost.

categories.title: Organize
categories.summary: Turn requirements into a backlog, and set out who does what.

categories.title: Improve

categories.title: Yours

cards.title: Plan it
cards.summary: Turn an ask into a checked plan of jobs, each with its risk and how it will be checked.
cards.outcome: A plan with its steps, risks and open questions, and each step as a job you can start.
useWhen: plan a larger piece of work
break an idea into jobs

cards.title: Build a feature
cards.summary: Clarify, design, build, review and test a change to your application.
cards.outcome: A pull request with the change, checked by tests and a review, after QE acceptance.
useWhen: add new behaviour to an app
a new screen, endpoint or option
a change that needs a design and tests

cards.title: Fix a bug
cards.summary: Find the cause of a bug, reproduce it, fix it and check that the fix holds.
cards.outcome: A pull request with the fix and the checks that show it holds, after QE acceptance.
useWhen: something is broken
an error or crash to fix
something that used to work no longer does

cards.title: Migrate or modernize
cards.summary: Change a shape in place: a schema, an API, a library, with expand, cutover and contract.
cards.outcome: A planned move with a confirmed cutover, proof the new path behaves like the old one, and the old path removed.
useWhen: move to a new library, service or schema
replace an old system step by step
a change that needs a cutover

options.title: Move
options.summary: Port to a new stack or platform; the old one is retired.

options.title: In place
options.summary: Change a shape in place: a schema, an API, a library, with expand, cutover and contract.

options.brief: Kind: upgrade. Move to the newer version named in the ask; the cutover is switching the pin, the cleanup removes compatibility shims.
options.title: Upgrade
options.summary: Move to a newer version of a dependency, framework or runtime.

cards.title: Refactor or polish
cards.summary: Restructure without changing behaviour.
cards.outcome: A pull request that restructures or tidies code with its behaviour unchanged, after QE acceptance.
useWhen: clean up or restructure code
rename or simplify without behaviour change

options.brief: Kind: polish. Small, safe quality fixes only; no restructuring.
options.title: Polish
options.summary: Small quality fixes: naming, dead code, lint, small UI fixes.

cards.title: Prepare a release
cards.summary: Check release readiness, bump versions and write the changelog in a pull request; never tags.
cards.outcome: A release pull request: versions bumped, changelog cut from what merged, and a GO or NO-GO readiness verdict.
useWhen: prepare the next release
bump versions and write the changelog

cards.title: Start something new
cards.summary: An HTTP or worker service.
cards.outcome: A new CLI, service, library or MCP server in a pull request, tested and reviewed; an MCP server is installed after your consent.
useWhen: start a new CLI, service or library
scaffold a new project

options.title: MCP server
options.summary: Tools for agents, installed after your consent.

cards.title: Studio plugin
cards.summary: Edit a kind of file in studio.
cards.outcome: A studio editor plugin designed, built, tested and installed after your consent.
useWhen: edit a new kind of file in studio
change how studio edits an artifact

options.title: Editor
options.summary: Edit a kind of file in studio.

options.statusNote: Plugging in your own step is not built yet.
options.title: Phase
options.summary: A new kind of step workflows can use.

cards.title: Plan tests
cards.summary: Write a risk-ranked test plan for a change or an area of the code, ready to automate.
cards.outcome: The test gaps in the code, then a risk-ranked test plan file in a pull request, ready to automate.
useWhen: decide what to test before building
a test strategy for a feature or release

cards.title: Test analysis (the gaps only)
cards.summary: Find the risky code with no tests, weak or flaky tests and what would close each gap, changing nothing.
cards.outcome: The existing test-analysis workflow, unchanged: the test gaps, without the plan.
useWhen: where are we under-tested
audit the quality of a test suite
find flaky or empty tests

cards.title: Write and run tests
cards.summary: Write tests for how existing code behaves and run them with the repository's own test setup.
cards.outcome: A pull request with behaviour tests that ran green under your own test setup.
useWhen: add missing tests
cover existing behaviour with tests

cards.title: Keep the suite healthy
cards.summary: Find and fix flaky, weak, stale-snapshot or slow tests without touching the code under test.
cards.outcome: A pull request that fixes flaky, weak, rotten or slow tests, with the suite run green under your own setup.
useWhen: fix flaky tests
strengthen weak tests
speed up a slow test suite

cards.title: Incident or root cause
cards.summary: Find the root cause of an incident from its error, logs and timeline, cited, changing nothing.
cards.outcome: What broke and why, each cause cited to a code or log line, with the fix handed to Bug.
useWhen: why did this break in production
find the root cause of an outage
explain this error from its logs

later.note: The source picker (ITSM, logs, the web you register) comes in 1.2. Today: paste the error, logs or timeline.

cards.statusNote: Coming in 1.2: it reads the web and other sources you register.
cards.title: Competitive or market analysis
cards.summary: How others do it, with every claim cited to a source.
cards.outcome: How others do it, with every claim cited to a source.

cards.statusNote: Coming in 1.1: it reads documents you upload.
cards.title: Due diligence
cards.summary: A cited review of a target's documents: what holds, what is missing, what is a risk.
cards.outcome: A cited review of a target's documents: what holds, what is missing, what is a risk.

cards.statusNote: Coming in 1.2: it reads the web and other sources you register.
cards.title: Research a question
cards.summary: A cited answer from outside sources.
cards.outcome: A cited answer from outside sources.

cards.title: Reconstruct what happened
cards.summary: Build a cited timeline of what changed and how it led to an outcome, changing nothing.
cards.outcome: A timeline of what changed and why, each event cited to a commit, pull request or run.
useWhen: what changed before this broke
reconstruct the history of a decision

cards.title: Analyze a codebase
cards.summary: Architecture and flows, cited (search narrate/service-map; engineering arch action).
cards.outcome: A cited account of the code: how it works, what it does as requirements, or where its docs are wrong.
useWhen: how does this part of the system work
map the flows and modules of a service

options.title: How it works
options.summary: Architecture and flows, cited (search narrate/service-map; engineering arch action).

options.title: Domain
options.summary: What the code does as requirements, with coverage. Writes its requirements map to the project graph, never the repository.

options.title: Docs vs code
options.summary: Every wrong or stale claim in the docs.

cards.title: Map requirements
cards.summary: Trace each requirement to the code and tests that satisfy it, and name what is missing.
cards.outcome: Each requirement you pick traced to the code that meets it, or marked unmet, cited.
useWhen: which requirements are implemented
build a traceability matrix

cards.statusNote: Coming in 1.1: it reads documents you upload.
cards.title: Analyze documents
cards.summary: What a set of documents says, compared and cited to the page.
cards.outcome: What a set of documents says, compared and cited to the page.

cards.statusNote: Comes once crew excludes the authors of every run that contributed to the change from its reviewers; today, Risk analysis or Security review read a change on a seat that did not build it.
cards.title: Review a change
cards.summary: Review a pull request, branch or commit and recommend approve, conditions or reject.
cards.outcome: A verdict on a pull request or branch: approve, conditional or reject, with every finding cited.
useWhen: review this pull request
is this change safe to merge

cards.statusNote: Coming in 1.1: it reads documents you upload.
cards.title: Critique a document, proposal or claim
cards.summary: Where an argument holds and where it does not, cited to the page.
cards.outcome: Where an argument holds and where it does not, cited to the page.

cards.title: Risk analysis
cards.summary: Assess the risks of a change or area from its blast radius, tests and churn, as a risk matrix.
cards.outcome: A risk matrix for a change or an area: failure modes, likelihood, impact and mitigations, cited.
useWhen: what could go wrong with this change
assess the risk of touching this code

cards.title: Security and compliance review
cards.summary: Review the code for vulnerabilities and weaknesses, each cited with its fix.
cards.outcome: Security, privacy or compliance findings, each cited to code, with the fix to make.
useWhen: review this code for security issues
check our attack surface

cards.title: Decide (ADR)
cards.summary: Lay out the options for a decision, score them with evidence, and record the option you pick.
cards.outcome: Options scored by seats that did not write them, and your pick; the ADR is then written by Document · Docs in the repo, filled in.
useWhen: choose between two or more approaches
write up an architecture decision

cards.title: Evaluate rules
